question.text: The sponsor of the Aravalli Long-Short Fund (a Category III AIF) has committed INR 12 crore as skin-in-the-game. Which of the following statements about this commitment is CORRECT under SEBI (AIF) Regulations?

answer.text: The sponsor can withdraw the commitment after 3 years from the date of first investment.
The commitment may be satisfied by waiving management fees of equivalent value.
The commitment applies only during the commitment period and lapses after final drawdown.
The commitment must be cash investment at par with other investors and cannot be withdrawn until all investor distributions are completed.

explanation.text: The Logic: Regulation mandates the sponsor/manager commitment be made as fresh cash investment, placed on par with other investors' risk, and remain locked in until distributions to all investors are completed in full. The sponsor is first in and last out. Waiver of management fees or transfer of stocks is explicitly disallowed as satisfaction of this commitment. The Trap: Option A invents a 3-year auto-release which does not exist. Option B is the classic shortcut managers try and the regulation specifically prohibits. Option C confuses the sponsor skin-in-game with the commitment-period drawdown concept. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C (All-Cat Manager) tests the same rule across categories. XIX-D tests it with Cat I/II 2.5%/5cr numbers. Distributor exams (XIX-B) frame it as investor-protection marketing language. Manager's Pro-Tip: When modelling sponsor cashflow IRR, remember the sponsor's INR 12 cr is effectively a perpetual subordination until the LAST rupee is distributed to LPs. Treat sponsor-IRR as strictly lower than LP-IRR in your internal waterfall models — this gap is why most Cat III managers also co-invest via a family-office vehicle that CAN exit earlier on the non-mandatory portion.
